items.title: Explore new ways to drive your best ROI with the first Google Marketing Platform Drop
items.excerpt: Google's first monthly Marketing Platform Drop adds a Display & Video 360 Marketplace where Gemini models curate personalized media bundles for live sports and tentpole events, activated in one click. It also adds a Search Ads 360 Home view that uses Gemini to consolidate insights, generate suggestions, and streamline execution.
items.note: Primary source. The published time comes from the RSS pubDate; the page only gives a date. The LinkedIn CTV-in-DV360 part overlaps adexchanger/ppc.land coverage from 10-22, but the Gemini-curated media bundles and SA360 Gemini home are the AI angle.

items.title: Meta delays its AI terms to November 20. The trust problem does not move
items.excerpt: Meta pushed the effective date of its revised Commercial Terms and Self-Serve Ad Terms from October 30 to November 20, 2026. These are the same terms that make advertisers solely liable for AI enhancements and give Meta broad AI-use rights over business content. Meta did not change the text, and EU and UK publisher and advertiser groups are still pressing regulators.
items.note: FOLLOW-UP to the covered story 'Meta Commercial Terms: advertisers solely liable for AI enhancements from Oct 30' (adweek, 10-23). The new fact is the delay to Nov 20. Use only as a date-change update. The Verge and Nieman Lab frame it from the publisher-scraping side, which is excluded.

items.title: New Studies Say AI Visibility & Search Not Worth Investing In
items.excerpt: Three studies published the same week find that AI search and chatbot services send a tiny share of traffic and conversions compared with Google Search. In Marie Haynes' GA4 data from 100 sites, ChatGPT sessions were 0.62% of Google organic. The studies question how much marketing budget should go to AI visibility work.
items.note: BORDERLINE: the angle is marketing budget for AI search, not paid placement. Keep only if the curator accepts the 'brand budget shifting to AI search' clause.

items.title: Google AI Overviews reach 88% of commercial searches as AI clicks stay thin
items.excerpt: Semrush tracked 400 US commercial keywords and found that AI Overviews now appear on 88% of them, and on 97% when weighted by search volume. A year earlier the figure was 45.75%. 'Reviews' queries rose from 30% to 89%. Referral traffic from AI stays tiny, and Ahrefs says Google is altering results served to SEO tools.
items.note: BORDERLINE: a daily roundup about the organic and commercial search surface. It overlaps the SER item, so pick at most one of the two.
